segments.label: Industrial Activities

metrics.label: Adjusted EBIT
metrics.note: Non-GAAP operating profitability; see CNH reconciliation.

metrics.label: Adjusted EBIT margin
metrics.note: Adjusted EBIT divided by Industrial Activities net sales.

metrics.label: Free cash flow
metrics.note: CNH-defined non-GAAP Industrial Activities cash measure.

segments.read: Read sales, operating margin, and cash together. Staffing actions can affect each on a different timetable.

segments.label: Agriculture
segments.read: Use the EBIT bridge below to separate demand and mix from pricing and cost.

segments.label: Construction
segments.read: Higher sales do not assure higher earnings. Confirm the cost and mix explanation before proposing a capacity change.

segments.label: Financial Services

metrics.label: Revenue
metrics.note: Financing business; keep this scope separate from Industrial Activities.

metrics.label: Net income
metrics.note: Segment net income, not segment adjusted EBIT.

metrics.label: Receivables >30 days past due
metrics.note: Share of the receivable balance past due.

segments.read: Financing supports equipment purchases. Credit quality and financing terms affect demand and risk.

segments.label: Industrial Activities

metrics.label: Free cash flow
metrics.note: Negative means cash used during H1.

segments.read: Q2 cash generation and first-half cash generation tell different stories. Do not substitute one period for the other.

segments.label: Agriculture
segments.read: Use the year-to-date view to test whether the latest quarter changes the broader trend.

segments.label: Construction
segments.read: Negative operating profit makes productivity, product cost, and investment timing especially relevant.

segments.label: Financial Services
segments.read: Keep Financial Services income separate from the equipment operations' EBIT and free cash flow.

items.name: Corn
items.driver: Price and saleable yield shape row-crop cash receipts; fertilizer, fuel, rent, and credit determine the margin.

items.name: Soybeans
items.driver: Crop margins and export demand influence replacement decisions for tractors, planting, and harvesting equipment.

items.name: Wheat
items.driver: Cash bids vary by wheat class and location. A national price outlook is one signal for grain-producer economics.

glossary.name: CNH Business System
glossary.definition: CNH's published operating approach includes daily management, strategy deployment, and kaizen.
glossary.question: Which workforce action changes a daily quality, delivery, safety, or cost measure?

glossary.name: Daily management
glossary.definition: Track operating measures and address gaps through a repeatable management routine.
glossary.question: Who owns the gap, the action, and the next check?

glossary.name: Continuous improvement
glossary.definition: Make and verify practical improvements to the way work is done.
glossary.question: Did the change reduce waste or improve good output?

glossary.name: Strategy deployment
glossary.definition: Connect strategic priorities to operating actions and measures.
glossary.question: How does this staffing or development action contribute to a business priority?

glossary.name: Industrial Activities
glossary.definition: CNH's enterprise scope excluding Financial Services.
glossary.question: Are you comparing equipment operating results with equipment operating results?

glossary.name: Adjusted earnings before interest and taxes
glossary.definition: CNH's non-GAAP profitability measure. Use the company reconciliation for the exact adjustments.
glossary.question: Which operating variance can our team influence?

glossary.name: Adjusted EBIT margin
glossary.definition: Adjusted EBIT divided by the matching net-sales measure.
glossary.question: Did profit change because of sales, product mix, or cost?

glossary.name: Basis points
glossary.definition: 100 basis points equals one percentage point.
glossary.question: Is the change in margin points or a percent change in the margin?

glossary.name: Volume & Mix
glossary.definition: An EBIT-bridge category showing the impact of sales volume and the composition of sales.
glossary.question: Does the product mix change required labor hours, skills, or margin?

glossary.name: Net pricing
glossary.definition: The net pricing contribution shown in CNH's EBIT bridge.
glossary.question: Is pricing enough to offset the other pressures?

glossary.name: Product Cost
glossary.definition: The EBIT-bridge cost category for products, including relevant manufacturing economics.
glossary.question: What changes cost per good unit: materials, labor, rework, or overhead?

glossary.name: Selling, general and administrative
glossary.definition: Selling and administrative expenses; distinguish them from factory product cost.
glossary.question: Where does this workforce cost sit in the P&L?

glossary.name: Research and development
glossary.definition: Spending to develop products and technology.
glossary.question: What future capability is being funded?

glossary.name: Foreign exchange / constant currency
glossary.definition: FX is currency impact; c.c. compares performance without currency translation movements.
glossary.question: Does reported growth also represent operating growth?

glossary.name: Free cash flow of Industrial Activities
glossary.definition: CNH's non-GAAP cash measure for the equipment operations. Read its reconciliation and period.
glossary.question: Does the proposal use cash now or release cash, and when?

glossary.name: Production hours
glossary.definition: A production-activity measure used in CNH's quarterly presentation.
glossary.question: What does the schedule imply for qualified hours, overhead, and flexibility?

glossary.name: Dealer / channel inventory
glossary.definition: Equipment held in the dealer channel; separate it from CNH factory inventory.
glossary.question: Are shipments supported by end-customer sell-through?

glossary.name: Production slots filled
glossary.definition: CNH's presentation indicates how booked the coming production periods are.
glossary.question: Are the slots sufficiently firm and matched to executable capacity?

glossary.name: Path to 2030
glossary.definition: CNH's published strategic framework for the business through 2030.
glossary.question: Which longer-term priority does this operating decision support?

glossary.name: Iron + Tech
glossary.definition: CNH's language for integrating equipment and technology.
glossary.question: Which manufacturing and service skills does the product require?

glossary.name: Fixed-cost under-absorption
glossary.definition: Lower activity leaves fixed manufacturing overhead spread across fewer units. Exact accounting depends on the costing method.
glossary.question: How do we manage the cost gap without building unsupported inventory?

glossary.name: Production constraint
glossary.definition: The process that limits completed output; spare capacity elsewhere cannot remove it.
glossary.question: Which role, process, or material actually limits shipments?

glossary.name: Qualified role coverage
glossary.definition: Role-by-role evidence of who can perform work at the required quality and level of independence.
glossary.question: Do we have enough qualified coverage on the required shifts?

glossary.name: FPY
glossary.definition: Share of units that pass the defined process the first time without rework.
glossary.question: How much scheduled output becomes good output?

glossary.name: Retail sales / wholesale shipments
glossary.definition: Retail reaches the end customer; wholesale supplies the dealer channel.
glossary.question: Is the demand signal customer purchases or inventory moving into the channel?

glossary.name: Operating working capital
glossary.definition: Inventory and receivables, less operating payables, are common drivers of cash tied up in operations.
glossary.question: What will happen to inventory, collection, and payment timing?

items.name: Built Around Customers
items.summary: Anticipate customer needs and help customers succeed.

items.name: We Go Beyond
items.summary: Keep improving quality and the way we work.

items.name: Make It Simple
items.summary: Make complex choices clear and practical.

items.name: Win As One
items.summary: Work together across teams and with partners.

items.name: You Matter
items.summary: Value people and support their shared growth.

industrial-activities.why: Separating equipment operations from financing makes the right margin and cash measures easier to use.

ebit-margin.why: Expressing the margin change in basis points gives the team one clear way to discuss performance.

volume-mix.why: Understanding the profit bridge helps Commercial, Manufacturing, Purchasing, Finance, and HR work on the same business problem.

industrial-fcf.why: Keeping quarter and year-to-date cash separate makes the financial position clearer before a decision.

industry-demand.why: Reading the market signal alongside orders and retail demand helps us plan around what customers actually need.

commodity-prices.why: Distinguishing a forecast from a market quote makes a complex commodity signal clearer and more useful.

farmer-economics.why: Understanding real purchasing power helps us anticipate the equipment decisions farmers can afford.

retail-wholesale.why: Checking end-customer demand helps us serve farmers instead of treating dealer shipments alone as customer success.

cyclicality.why: Commercial, Operations, Finance, and HR can prepare the recovery together using shared demand signals.

skills-capacity.why: Developing qualified skills at the constraint invests in people and helps them contribute to reliable output.

absorption.why: Making fixed cost per unit visible helps the team understand the tradeoff and choose a clear response.

dealer-inventory.why: Matching production to genuine customer demand supports the right equipment availability without loading the channel.

ramp-readiness.why: A credible ramp brings together qualified people, materials, quality, and the production plan.

downcycle.why: Using a downcycle to develop useful skills invests in people’s growth and future opportunities.

cbs.why: Daily management and continuous improvement connect our capabilities to better quality, delivery, and cost.

product-cost.why: Judging staffing by good output, quality, and total cost supports better performance than wages alone.

capex.why: HR, Operations, and Finance can agree on the training baseline and validate the benefit together.

working-capital.why: Reducing rework and improving flow advances quality and performance while freeing cash for the business.

fallback.why: Turning business information into a clear, practical decision could support Make It Simple.
